text: Loughcrew is a great megalithic burial center in County Meath, near the middle of Ireland. Its Irish name, Sliab na Cailleach, means mountain of the hag, and legend ties the site to the great hag the Cailleach. Several hills make up the Loughcrew complex, holding passage graves and other ritual places. The stone is rich in carved ornament, with spirals, starbursts, and meanders cut into the granite. On one hillside sits the Hag's Chair, a seat made of rocks from which a person can see several distant counties. Atop that hill a decorated cairn faces the sunrise at the spring and fall equinox.

okr.objective: Document Loughcrew as a megalithic burial center tied to the hag Cailleach.
